summary: A choice from a closed list, in three sizes and three shapes, with an optional icon on the trigger and an avatar per option.

props.name: options
props.description: The choices. `value` and `label` are required; `description` and `avatar` are optional per option. The shape is fixed rather than generic because you own the file: data that does not fit is an edit to the option body, not an API.

props.name: description
props.description: A line under the control, for context on what the choice means.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Shown on the trigger before anything is selected.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: The option selected when you are not controlling it. Pair `value` with `onValueChange` instead if you are.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Called with the newly selected value, or `null` if the selection was cleared. Required for a controlled select.

props.name: icon
props.description: A single icon fixed on the trigger, not per option. For the per-option kind, give an option an `avatar` instead.

props.name: iconPosition
props.description: Which side `icon` sits on. Trailing sits just before the chevron.

props.name: size
props.description: Height and width of the trigger. The popup follows it.

props.name: shape
props.description: Corner radius, applied to the trigger and the popup together. `squircle` uses `corner-shape`.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Blocks interaction and dims the whole control, label included.

props.name: required
props.description: Appends a red asterisk to the label & sets the trigger's native `required` attribute.

props.name: animated
props.description: Fades and scales the popup in and out. Turn it off for a static popup, or when the user has asked for reduced motion.

props.name: focus
props.description: The focus outline. `true` draws it, `false` removes it along with the danger, error and success tints that ride with it, and a string of Yumma CSS utilities restyles it on every focusable part of the component, which is more than `className` reaches. Removing it outright and putting nothing back fails WCAG 2.4.7.

props.name: container
props.description: Where the popup is rendered. Defaults to `document.body`, which is right almost always; pass an element to portal somewhere else, such as inside a frame or a container that owns its own stacking context.
